one_liner: I worked on Capital One Travel across several phases of the product, contributing to components and pages that needed to support new content and new priorities as the platform grew. One ongoing challenge was expanding the site as Capital One opened new airport lounges. My work focused on building templates and components that made it possible to roll out new lounge pages without reinventing the structure each time. The goal was to create UI that felt cohesive, stable, and simple to extend as new locations launched.

problem.summary: Capital One Travel evolved through many short development cycles, often with different teams contributing at different times.  When new lounges opened, each page needed its own content and layout, but it also had to feel like part of the same experience. The challenge was working within the patterns that existed while strengthening the areas where the system had started to drift.

goals: Build templates and components that supported new lounge pages
Make new work feel like part of the existing system
Work with what the system already provides
Make the product easier to extend
Strengthen reusable pieces and leave the system more predictable
responsibilities: Built components and layouts that could support the platform as it expanded
Shaped new pages for lounge launches
Refined existing patterns so future contributors could work more smoothly
Understood how the system behaved, which parts were reliable, and where updates would make the experience more consistent
Made thoughtful adjustments to the interface so new additions felt natural
outcomes: Made the site easier to update as new lounges and new content rolled out
Reduced the amount of one-off development needed for each launch
Improved interface consistency across different pages
Aligned spacing rules to reduce design and engineering drift
Reused interaction patterns to give QA fewer variations to track
Cleaned up older components to make the system more predictable
